newsitem.title: USA: Metal Recovery to raise zinc production.
newsitem.headline: Metal Recovery to raise zinc production.

text.p: Metal Recovery Technologies Inc said a second electrowinning cell has been built at its East Chicago, Indiana plant to raise zinc production from half a ton a day to two tons per day.
The 99.8 percent grade zinc is recovered from processing galvanized scrap into black scrap for steelmakers at the company's facility.
"Currently we are selling zinc to Detriot-based North American Zinc Corp for use in galvanizing and zinc alloy production," said Michael Lucas, Metal Recovery's chairman.

"Also, as our earlier economic predictions indicated, our black scrap by-product is currently being sold at a $26 per ton premium over number one dealer bundles and, as supply becomes more reliable, we expect premiums to rise to $30 per ton."
A project between Metal Recovery and University of California at Berkeley is trying to cut power consumption in the electrowinning facility.
The research shows promise of a major cut in energy and the ability to increase the amount of zinc recovered.
